$comment: Trust score weights and curves (D1-06). Calibrated against the real ranges D1-05 measured
across all 30 sandbox cameras, not invented. docs/trust-score.md section 3 carries the
This file is config, not code: the acceptance criterion is that changing a weight changes the
scores with no code change, and trust-score.test.ts proves it by scoring identical signals
THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: a signal that cannot be judged is excluded from the denominator,
never scored zero. Unmeasurable is not bad. See `applicability` on each signal.

bands.$comment: Ticket-specified. trusted >= 70, degraded 40-69, untrusted < 40, dead = unreachable.

$rationale: A camera that cannot be reached contributes nothing, so this must carry weight — but 20,
not the 30 it started at, because of what this signal actually does in practice.
An unreachable camera is banded `dead` before any arithmetic runs, so for every camera
that reaches the scorer this signal is full marks. Its weight is therefore a FLOOR that
every working camera collects for free. At 30 that floor was too generous: cam22, whose
blur of 0.011 means it can produce no readable image at all, still scored 60 — a camera
that answers the phone should not be five-eighths of the way to trusted.
Scored 0 when connectable but not decodable: answering the phone is not the same as
being usable.
The heaviest weight, because focus is the signal that most directly decides whether this
camera can do the job at all: an out-of-focus camera produces no plate reads no matter how
reliably it answers.
LOG scale, and this is the point D1-05's handoff is emphatic about: blur_score spans
0.011 to 5794.088 across this estate — five orders of magnitude. On a linear map the
estate MEDIAN of 298.6 would score 5% of full marks and almost every working camera
would read as broken.
floor 10.0: below this the image carries no detectable structure. cam22 (0.011) and
cam09 (2.047) are the two real cameras under it, and both are independently unusable.

target 250.0: the level at which focus stops being the limiting factor. Set just BELOW
        the measured estate median of 298.6 on purpose - putting the target exactly at the median
        would leave half the estate short of full marks for being typical.
Half an estate being useless after dark, with nobody knowing which half, is exactly the
blindness this pillar exists to expose.
darkMax 40.0: effectively black, scored zero. The recording runs ~21:00-09:00 and the
measured night frames sit near luma 90 — this estate is streetlit, not pitch dark, so a
threshold that fired on darkness would condemn most of it for most of its footage.
cam09 (8.40) and cam07 (38.22) are the two real cameras below it.
usableMin 60.0: full marks above this. The measured median is 92.7, so a typical camera
is comfortably clear and the ramp only bites on genuinely dim ones.
blownMin 235.0: a lamp or headlight staring into the lens is as unreadable as darkness.
Occlusion, freezing and spray paint. Weighted below focus and light because on this
estate it is the rarest failure: 24 of 30 cameras measured exactly 0.000.
cleanMax 0.05 / severeMin 0.35 are RE-DERIVED from measured data, which BL-01 assigned to
this ticket. The prober's own display flag sits at 0.60 and NOTHING on a real estate
reached it — the observed maximum is 0.388. A bar nothing can clear is not a detector.
0.33 puts BOTH genuinely degraded cameras (cam22 at 0.388, cam09 at 0.335) at or past
full penalty, where they belong, while 24 clean cameras at 0.000 are untouched.
This curve is the trust score's own; the prober's flag is a separate display concern and
is deliberately not changed from another ticket's worker.
Two things at once: is the rate adequate for ANPR, and did the department's claim match.
adequateMin 12.0: below roughly 12 fps a vehicle crossing the frame yields too few
candidate frames for multi-frame plate voting (D2-01). Six real cameras sit under it,
cam30 lowest at 4.36.
unusableMax 4.0: at or below this a vehicle can cross the scene between frames.
divergencePenalty 0.5: halves this signal when measured and declared disagree by more
than the prober's threshold. A penalty, not a zero — a camera running at half its claimed
rate is still a working camera, it is the REGISTRY that is wrong, and the delta is
reported as a registry-accuracy finding rather than pretending the lens is at fault.
On this estate every declared_fps is NULL because the catalogue supplies only {id,name},
so nothing is currently penalised here — a camera whose owner declared nothing cannot be
caught lying, and that ABSENCE is itself the Pillar 1 finding.
A camera with a wrong clock corrupts every route reconstruction it contributes to — it is
the one signal whose failure poisons OTHER cameras' answers rather than only its own,
which is why it carries weight despite being inapplicable here.
applicability live-only, and this is load-bearing: on a VOD source the same arithmetic
measures how fast the file was pulled. D1-05 measured 24,505 to 161,162 ms across this
estate — that is the gateway throttling, not thirty broken clocks.
Every sandbox row is VOD, so this weight is EXCLUDED from the denominator and the
remaining 90 are renormalised to 100. It is not scored as a loss. Scoring it would mean
every camera silently forfeits 10 points for being a recording behind a slow link.
